overview: Every other IMU in this encyclopedia hands you raw accelerometer/gyroscope/magnetometer numbers and leaves the hard part — sensor fusion — to your code. The BNO055 is different: it contains its own dedicated ARM Cortex-M0 microcontroller that runs the accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer fusion internally, and simply reports a ready-to-use orientation (as Euler angles or a quaternion) over I2C. That's a genuinely different category of chip — a 'smart sensor' rather than a raw-data sensor — and it's the reason people choose it despite costing more than an MPU6050/9250: no Kalman filter or Madgwick filter to write, tune, or debug.
simpleSummary: An all-in-one motion sensor that does its own math and just tells you your exact orientation in space.

specifications.internalProcessor: ARM Cortex-M0, runs onboard sensor fusion
specifications.outputFormats: Absolute orientation (Euler angles or quaternion), linear acceleration, gravity vector, calibration status
specifications.fusionModes: NDOF (9-DOF fused), IMU (6-DOF, no magnetometer), and several other selectable modes

pinMap.name: PS0
pinMap.function: Protocol select bit 0 — both PS0/PS1 LOW selects I2C mode (the default on most breakouts).

pinMap.name: RST
pinMap.function: Active-LOW reset — resets the internal fusion processor.

pinMap.name: INT
pinMap.function: Interrupt output, configurable for several fusion/sensor events.

useCases.title: Robot/drone orientation without writing a fusion filter
useCases.scenario: Read ready-made orientation output directly, skipping the usual Kalman/Madgwick filter development.

useCases.title: Camera gimbal stabilization
useCases.scenario: Fast, stable orientation data feeding directly into a stabilization control loop.

useCases.title: VR/AR orientation tracking
useCases.scenario: Onboard fusion reduces the host processor's workload for real-time head tracking.

oftenConfusedWith: MPU6050/MPU9250 (raw sensor data, fusion left to your own code)
oftenUpgradedTo: Dedicated flight-controller-grade AHRS units for aviation-certified accuracy
